title: Count matching lines in a CSV file
description:
Write a function `count_lines_containing(path, keyword, exclude=None)` that reads the `hacker_news.csv` file at `path` and counts how many rows have `keyword` (case-insensitive) in their `title` column. If `exclude` is given, skip rows whose title also contains it.

Covers all 3 sub-parts of source item 6 (Python mentions, JavaScript mentions, Java-but-not-JavaScript mentions) as one exercise. `hacker_news.csv` (2000 real Hacker News posts) is available in your working directory.

hints: csv.DictReader(file) reads each row as a dict keyed by the header row's column names, so row['title'] gets you the title text directly, without tracking column positions by hand.
Open the file with csv.DictReader, count rows where keyword.lower() is in row['title'].lower(), and additionally skip a row when exclude is given and also found in that same title.
expected_behavior: Returns the count of rows whose title contains keyword, minus any that also contain exclude.

hidden_tests.label: source item 6, part 3: java but not javascript

explanation: csv.DictReader turns the header row into dict keys automatically, so the code reads 'the title column' as row['title'] instead of a numeric index that would break if the CSV's column order ever changed.
